questions.question: A new SSD connects over PCIe lanes instead of a SATA cable and sustains 5 GB/s sequential reads. Which storage protocol replaced AHCI for such drives?
questions.explanation: NVMe runs SSDs over PCIe with a lean queue-based protocol, far beyond AHCI/SATA limits.

questions.question: Rows of chokes and MOSFETs beside the CPU socket step the PSU's 12 V down to about 1.2 V and hold it steady through sudden load spikes. Which motherboard component is this?
questions.explanation: The VRM converts and regulates the PSU's 12 V rail into the CPU's low core voltage.

questions.question: A 6-core CPU shows 12 logical processors because each core keeps two sets of architectural state feeding one execution pipeline. Which Intel technology is this?
questions.explanation: Hyper-Threading (Intel's SMT) duplicates architectural state so each physical core hosts two threads.

questions.question: A RAM stick's datasheet says it moves data on both the rising and falling edge of every clock, doubling throughput without doubling the clock rate. Which SDRAM technology is this?
questions.explanation: DDR (Double Data Rate) SDRAM transfers twice per clock cycle — on both edges.

questions.question: On an older motherboard, USB, SATA, and audio attach to a slower companion chip linked to the northbridge, while RAM and PCIe lanes connect to the faster one. Name the I/O chip.
questions.explanation: The southbridge handled slower I/O; modern boards merged its role into the PCH.

questions.question: A gamer connects two NVIDIA cards with a bridge connector so they split frame rendering for a single monitor. Which multi-GPU technology is this?
questions.explanation: SLI links NVIDIA GPUs to share rendering work; AMD's equivalent was CrossFire.

questions.question: A brownout lasts three seconds, yet the file server stays up and logs the event, powered by a battery-backed box between the wall outlet and the PSU. What device provided the ride-through?
questions.explanation: A UPS supplies instant battery power through outages and brownouts.

questions.question: A CPU with flat gold contact pads drops into a socket whose delicate spring-loaded pins live on the motherboard itself. Which socket style is this?
questions.explanation: LGA puts the pins in the socket and pads on the CPU — the reverse of PGA.

questions.question: A rebuilt PC idles 15 °C hotter until the builder fills the microscopic gaps between the CPU's heat spreader and the heatsink base with a gray compound. What was applied?
questions.explanation: Thermal paste displaces insulating air between the heat spreader and the heatsink.

questions.question: A CPU listed at 3.0 GHz sustains 4.4 GHz in short bursts when only a few cores are active and thermal headroom allows, then returns to base. Which feature is responsible?
questions.explanation: Turbo Boost (Intel; Precision Boost on AMD) opportunistically raises clocks above the base rate.

questions.question: A power supply rated 80% efficient delivers 400 W to the components under load. How much power does it draw from the wall outlet?
questions.explanation: 400 W divided by 0.8 efficiency equals 500 W drawn; the extra 100 W is lost as heat inside the PSU.

questions.question: A DDR5-6000 memory kit runs at only 4800 MT/s after installation. Which BIOS/UEFI feature must be enabled to reach the rated speed?
questions.explanation: XMP (Intel) or EXPO (AMD) profiles apply the kit's rated speeds and timings; without them RAM falls back to slower JEDEC defaults.

questions.question: Two identical RAM sticks are installed in the alternating slots the manual specifies, letting the memory controller access both simultaneously. Which feature does this enable?
questions.explanation: Dual-channel interleaves access across two memory channels, roughly doubling memory bandwidth versus single-channel.

questions.question: Before a graphics card needs its 6-pin or 8-pin power cables, how many watts can the PCIe x16 slot itself supply?
questions.explanation: The PCIe slot delivers up to 75 W; cards exceeding that require supplementary power connectors.

questions.question: A PC refuses to boot after upgrading to a newer CPU on an older but socket-compatible motherboard. Which update most often adds support for the new processor?
questions.explanation: Newer CPUs typically require a BIOS/UEFI update containing their microcode before the board can initialize them.
